A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Magical study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures, and the added v2 checklist, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, representation analyses, sensitivity tests, and a generated-text case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original expert evaluations, model-based ratings, baseline comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and transfer experiments.

M1.justification: The core asymmetric architecture, contrastive objective, and switching mechanism remain unchanged. Appendix E.9 adds a transfer procedure that freezes A learned on the original datasets and trains a newly initialized B on EASI, constituting a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained Cochrane, eLife, and Plos_genetics datasets, v2 evaluates medical transfer on EASI, labeled ESAI in Table 12, and legal summarization on IN-Abs, IN-Ext, and UK-Abs in Table 13. This substantially expands domain and test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparator set remains. v2 adds full-parameter fine-tuning across the three existing backbones in Table 9 and prompted o3-mini in Table 10, introducing substantially different comparison methods beyond the original prompt and LoRA-variant evaluations.

E3.justification: New protocols include full-test-set 1–10 ratings by o3-mini and DeepSeek-R1, anonymized evaluation by two experts of 20 examples per dataset, and BERTScore evaluation. Appendix E.9 also introduces source-to-target transfer controls and frozen-A adaptation. Existing splits, training budgets, and Appendix C settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 retains the original ablations, router analysis, recommendation-error tests, and rank sensitivity study. It adds sensitivity to K = 8, 16, 24, and 32, EASI distribution-shift and transfer analysis, and a legal case examining confusion between a party's argument and a court's conclusion.

E5.justification: The new checklist states that experimental results were tested multiple times, information absent from v1. It supplies no run count, seeds, or additional uncertainty estimates or significance tests; this disclosure does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Original results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–7 are retained, while Tables 6–13 add substantial findings. For example, Cochrane expert ratings are 8.55/8.35 for Magical versus 6.90/7.10 for LoRA. New legal results generally favor Magical, with UK-Abs ROUGE-1 lower than rsLoRA, 38.72 versus 38.84. These are additional comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the existing mathematical definitions remain unchanged. The new appendix material adds empirical studies and explanations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about semantic fidelity, diverse lay-style generation, asymmetric adaptation, and 31.66% fewer trainable parameters. The added experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E.9 adds an important applicability distinction between failure on truly unseen lay styles and successful supervised transfer of frozen A, attributing transferability to separating summarization from style. v2 also explains the K-selection tradeoff and proposes interpreting EHR predictions as future work. The missing-recommender limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link on the title page and describes implementation of the frozen-A/new-B transfer experiment. Existing hardware, optimizer, dataset counts, and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged. Repository availability beyond the supplied link is unverified.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning health AI, activation steering, EHR analysis, and legal summarization, and replaces several references, including Octavius with RankExpert in the routing discussion. The central positioning relative to LoRA and HydraLoRA remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Existing prose and the main section sequence are largely retained. Edits include expanded affiliations and correspondence labels, updated venue information, acknowledgements, a checklist, a short EHR discussion, and Appendix E expansion that moves the case-study subsection from E.4 to E.10.

P2.justification: v2 introduces nine substantial table displays: Tables 6–13 and 15. The original medical case table is retained and relocated as Table 14. Figures 1–7 and the original numerical tables retain their content, alongside title-page and text-flow adjustments.

improvement.justification: v1 supported generated-text quality mainly through overlap metrics, activation visualizations, and one case. v2 adds anonymized expert assessment, full-test-set model ratings, and BERTScore, substantially addressing that evidence gap. Additional baseline and transfer experiments strengthen comparative evidence and clarify applicability. The small expert study, incomplete evaluation details, and limited uncertainty reporting constrain confidence, but the net gain in empirical support is substantial.
